source.verification_method: All twelve supplied pages, all four numbered tables, both vignette specification tables and complete bibliography read. Pages 7, 8 and 10 visually inspected. Publisher/Crossref and university profiles verify identity/date/names; selected bibliography DOI checks are metadata-only. Statistical audit checks rounded summaries without original data or code.

citation.title: Resource allocation by algorithms: people prefer almost any alternative

reading.source_scope_note: A randomized 5 × 5 between-subject vignette survey retains 1,433 of 1,680 participants. Humans rate the moral desirability of one person receiving one good through a friend, waiting list, lottery, market or unspecified AI procedure. It measures evaluations, perceived comprehensibility and utilitarian attitudes, not actual allocation quality, adoption, model conduct or moral truth. Opacity is a measured post-outcome correlate, not an experimentally isolated cause.
access_limits: Complete supplied article and bibliography read; no substantive figures are present. All four numbered tables and two vignette lists read, with rendered visual confirmation of main and regression tables.

The inspected publisher page has no Supplementary section located. Its Data availability statement also says no datasets were generated or analysed despite the described experiment. No raw data, analysis code, registration, complete fielded questionnaire, allocation seed or exclusion-by-condition flow was obtained. No author was contacted.

Publisher table-4 URL was unavailable through the web tool; the supplied PDF table was visually inspected directly. This does not prevent reading the supplied table or prove that no alternate public rendering exists.

Primary name verification: https://econ-ethics.uni-hohenheim.de/en/michaelhaiden and https://econ-ethics.uni-hohenheim.de/en/sitemap show Michael Haiden and Prof. Dr. Matthias Uhl. No contact information is needed for this review.

Kahane et al. 2018 DOI 10.1037/rev0000093 and corrected Wachter et al. 2017 DOI 10.1093/idpl/ipx005 were metadata-verified, not independently fully read here. DOI 10.1609/aimag.v38i3.2741 identifies a different Goodman/Flaxman article. Other books, legal interpretations and philosophical originals remain secondary sources.

No private access, author-code execution, full-paper Markdown archive, participant-level data or independent replication. Resource vignettes are research stimuli, not medical, legal or public-benefit allocation advice.

study.sample: CloudResearch Prime Panels: 1,680 participants, 247 control-question exclusions, 1,433 retained. Mean age 47.13, SD 16.78; 892 female, 528 male, 13 otherwise. Recruitment country, representativeness, power analysis, control-question wording, exclusion breakdown and per-cell Ns are not reported. Do not assume a representative US sample solely from platform or political response wording.
study.design: Random assignment to one of 25 good × mechanism vignettes. Goods: kidney, kindergarten place, lawyer after wrongful accusation, shelter after hurricane, theater tickets. Mechanisms: friend, waiting list, lottery, market, AI-based algorithmic procedure. Each participant evaluates exactly one vignette; this is not a within-person preference ranking or actual algorithm use.
study.bundles: Names, gender, urgency narrative, beneficiaries and life context vary across goods. Mechanism labels are minimally specified; friend need not mean expert human judgment and can suggest favoritism, while market/list/lottery are procedures rather than alternative persons. No accuracy, price, eligibility, transparency, appeal, discretion or resource-scarcity outcome is equated or manipulated.
study.outcomes: Moral desirability on 0–6, followed by a single easy-to-understand item on 0–6, then Oxford Utilitarianism Scale and demographics. Only a successful recipient is described; displaced recipients and distributions are not observed. These measures do not identify a fair allocation rule, objectively correct judgment or actual take-up behavior.
study.desirability: Pooled means: friend 4.830, waiting list 4.883, lottery 3.986, market 4.388, algorithm 3.863. Ten pairwise independent-samples tests use Bonferroni adjustment. Algorithm is lower than friend/list/market, but not significantly different from lottery. All pooled means exceed the 0–6 midpoint, so relative disadvantage does not by itself establish absolute moral rejection.
study.effects: Approximate standardized differences from rounded means/SDs match reported magnitudes: friend versus algorithm about .586, waiting list versus algorithm .604, market versus algorithm .289, lottery versus algorithm .065. Exact weighted pooled-SD effects and adjusted p values cannot be reconstructed without Ns/raw data. Preserve supported contrasts rather than treat all reporting errors as invalidating the experiment.
study.mixed_model: Algorithm-versus-all-other-mechanisms coefficient −.657, SE .116, t −5.667, p < .001, with good random intercept. The comparator pools four substantively different procedures. Five good levels limit generalization across resource domains, and ordinal single-item outcomes are treated linearly.
study.comprehensibility: Algorithm label predicts lower perceived ease of understanding, b −.894, SE .110. Higher ease correlates with desirability, b .480, SE .024; adding it reduces the algorithm coefficient to −.238, p .025. Source calls this pattern consistent with partial explanation. Post-outcome measured opacity is not randomized: common causes, evaluative halo and reverse direction remain possible. Coefficient attenuation alone is not a causal mediation analysis or proof that explanation provision repairs aversion.
study.essentiality: Kidney and shelter are classified essential for survival; kindergarten, lawyer and theater nonessential. Formal interaction b .494, SE .235, t 2.103, p .036 indicates a smaller relative algorithm disadvantage for the essential group. This is a real reported interaction, not merely subgroup significance. But essentiality is bundled with five specific stories, not independently randomized within each good. Access to a lawyer or childcare can be consequential even under this study’s binary classification.
study.simple_contrast: Reported nonessential algorithm coefficient −.861 plus interaction .494 implies an essential contrast −.367. Without coefficient covariance, no exact simple-effect standard error or significance can be recovered. Main essentiality p .509 does not prove equality or that importance never matters.
study.utilitarianism: OUS distinguishes impartial beneficence from instrumental harm. IB coefficient .122, SE .043, p .005 is a nonalgorithm-reference conditional main effect, not a significant algorithm-specific moderator. IH main effect p .298; IB × algorithm p .475; IH × algorithm p .145. No significant interactions establish that either trait uniquely reduces algorithm aversion. Nonsignificance is not evidence of zero association or trait equivalence.
study.demographics: Age main coefficient −.008, p .020 applies at the nonalgorithm reference, with age × algorithm p .087. Fully adjusted algorithm coefficient −1.688 is conditional on zero-valued covariates and reference levels, not a population-average adjusted disadvantage. Covariate centering is unreported; do not interpret it as an effect for a typical adult.
study.reporting: Table 4 education estimate −.316 / SE .036 gives about −8.78, not reported t +.90; politics +.351 / .033 gives +10.64, not reported t −1.07. These sign/magnitude conflicts exceed ordinary rounding. Correct values cannot be inferred as exact output. Small differences in other rounded ratios, especially age, are not automatically errors.
study.philosophy: Reflective equilibrium, capability theory, liberty, justice and embedded values are discussed as normative frameworks. Folk algorithmics is a proposed research program, not a newly demonstrated mental behavior. Public attitudes may affect political feasibility without determining moral truth; source explicitly separates this practical question from the truth of a moral theory.
study.scope: No actual AI policy, optimization, model accuracy, efficiency, real discrimination, behavioral reliance, intervention on transparency or clinical/legal outcome was tested. Broad universal human preference, irrational aversion and evolutionary origin of these views are not established by this survey.

summary: No new record. Enrich existing algorithm aversion, two utilitarian-attitude facets and the background definition of reflective equilibrium; add non-counted fairness/utilitarian-reasoning context. Retain randomized label comparisons and the formal essentiality interaction while separating preference from moral correctness and post-outcome opacity from causal mediation. Document author-name reversal, wrong bibliography DOI, demographic percentage, impossible printed coefficients and contradictory data statement.

findings.definition: Reluctance to use or accept algorithmic judgments or decisions relative to human judgment in a comparable task.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named construct already exists. Preserve moral attitudes, normative methods and actual behavior as distinct outcomes; do not rename a new allocation context as a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Randomized allocation-label vignettes yield lower pooled moral-desirability ratings for an unspecified AI procedure than friend, waiting list and market, but not lottery. A formal interaction reports less relative disadvantage in the two essential-good vignettes.
findings.boundary: Preference ratings are not actual use, demonstrated irrationality or evidence of inferior algorithm quality. The four comparator labels are not all equivalent human judgment. All pooled means exceed scale midpoint; no equivalence with lottery is proven. Measured opacity and five bundled good narratives do not isolate a unique cause.

findings.definition: Giving equal moral weight to people’s welfare without privileging oneself or those to whom one is especially close.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named construct already exists. Preserve moral attitudes, normative methods and actual behavior as distinct outcomes; do not rename a new allocation context as a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The source defines impartial concern and uses the OUS IB subscale. Higher IB has a positive conditional association with nonalgorithm-reference moral-desirability ratings; its interaction with algorithm label is not significant.
findings.boundary: Do not interpret a nonalgorithm main effect as evidence that beneficence uniquely makes people accept AI. Attitude score, actual helping, normative truth and a model’s benevolent feeling are distinct. Exact administered items, reliability and missingness are not supplied.

findings.definition: Accepting harm to an innocent person as a means to producing greater aggregate welfare.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named construct already exists. Preserve moral attitudes, normative methods and actual behavior as distinct outcomes; do not rename a new allocation context as a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The source distinguishes willingness to accept harm for aggregate welfare from impartial concern and measures the OUS IH subscale. Neither its conditional main effect nor algorithm interaction reaches conventional significance in the reported model.
findings.boundary: A null coefficient does not show that harm attitudes never matter, equal beneficence or justify enacted harm. No actual harmful allocation or model moral reasoning is measured. Preserve this facet separately from broad utilitarianism.

findings.definition: A method of mutually revising considered judgments and guiding principles until they form a coherent, provisionally justified set.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named construct already exists. Preserve moral attitudes, normative methods and actual behavior as distinct outcomes; do not rename a new allocation context as a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Background discussion describes balancing considered judgments with theory until a provisional equilibrium, and reports philosophical objections to relying on intuitions.
findings.boundary: This is a secondary conceptual account, not an experimental test of a deliberation procedure or proof that coherence identifies moral truth. Current respondents did not iteratively revise judgments and principles.

findings.definition: Evaluating whether the rules, evidence and procedures used to reach a decision are fair, rather than assessing only its outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named construct already exists. Preserve moral attitudes, normative methods and actual behavior as distinct outcomes; do not rename a new allocation context as a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Participants evaluate receiving a good through different named allocation mechanisms; procedural justice motivates the study.
findings.boundary: Context only:the measured item is overall moral desirability, not a validated separate process-fairness scale or audit of the actual procedure. Labels leave criteria, opportunity to appeal, error and discrimination unspecified.

findings.definition: Evaluating whether the outcomes or allocations produced by a decision are fair.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named construct already exists. Preserve moral attitudes, normative methods and actual behavior as distinct outcomes; do not rename a new allocation context as a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The normative background discusses fair allocation and the survey asks about one successful recipient.
findings.boundary: Context only:no complete distribution, competing claimants or dedicated outcome-fairness measure is supplied. Do not infer distributive justice or actual inequity from a single recipient’s vignette approval.

findings.definition: Evaluating available actions by their expected aggregate effects on the well-being of those affected, with the aim of producing the greatest overall benefit.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named construct already exists. Preserve moral attitudes, normative methods and actual behavior as distinct outcomes; do not rename a new allocation context as a new independent mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper separates impartial beneficence and instrumental harm rather than treating utilitarianism as one psychological dimension.
findings.boundary: Context only:trait endorsement is not observed aggregate-welfare calculation or demonstrated actual/model reasoning. Efficiency assumptions and public approval do not settle which allocation is justified.

source_corrections.finding: Publisher and Crossref reverse given/family-name order into Haiden Michael and Uhl Matthias. Institutional profiles identify Michael Haiden and Matthias Uhl. Store corrected display names while documenting original metadata; this is not a different author pair.

The cited IDPL 7(2):76–99 title belongs to DOI 10.1093/idpl/ipx005. Printed DOI 10.1609/aimag.v38i3.2741 instead identifies Goodman and Flaxman, European Union Regulations on Algorithmic Decision Making and a Right to Explanation, AI Magazine 38(3):50–57. Correct the reference identity without claiming full reading or providing a current legal ruling.
Thirteen of 1,433 is approximately 0.91%, not less than 0.1%. The gender counts sum correctly to 1,433; this small percentage error does not change the sample total.

source_corrections.location: PDF 10 Table 4 education and politics rows
source_corrections.finding: Printed education −.316, SE .036 is incompatible in sign and magnitude with t +.90, p .370. Politics +.351, SE .033 is incompatible with t −1.07, p .284. These are visually confirmed table inconsistencies. Raw output is unavailable, so do not invent corrected coefficients or infer significant demographics from the erroneous printed ratios.

The statement that no datasets were generated or analysed conflicts with the original 1,680-participant experiment and statistical analyses described. This is a contradictory availability statement, not evidence that the study was never conducted or that data cannot exist.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: No public dataset/code/registration or full questionnaire was located on the inspected publisher page. Missing per-cell Ns, control-check wording, exclusion flow, exact model formula/estimation and complete-case Ns prevent full reconstruction. Absence from inspected materials is not proof that no materials exist elsewhere.

The single comprehensibility item is collected after moral desirability, with no independent transparency manipulation. Reverse association or common appraisal may explain coefficient attenuation; causal mediation and explanation-based remedies remain untested.

Two versus three heterogeneous good vignettes carry the essentiality contrast. The formal interaction is reported, but identity, named/gendered beneficiary and story-specific meaning are bundled. Five random-intercept levels do not establish a general law about essential resources.

Recruitment jurisdiction, representative weighting, prior AI experience and algorithm competence assumptions are unreported. A single moral-desirability rating is not observed adoption, individual ranking or a transparent estimate of widespread absolute rejection.

The introduction makes broad interpretive claims about opacity, legal rights and philosophical positions. Their originals were not fully verified here; do not import them as current law or universal facts. The verified bibliography DOI correction is separate from their substantive truth.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Essentiality claim based only on subgroup significance
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: A formal mechanism × essentiality interaction is reported, p .036. Preserve it while limiting its causal meaning to bundled vignette conditions.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: All contrasts and sample counts fail arithmetic
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: 1,680 minus 247 equals 1,433; exclusion rate 14.7% and gender count total reconcile. Approximate standardized differences reproduce Table 2 magnitudes. Isolate the demographic percentage and Table 4 row errors.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Label Review means no empirical study
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Despite the journal label, the supplied paper reports original randomized vignettes and analyses. The contradictory data statement does not justify discarding those reported methods as nonexistent.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Algorithm and lottery are proven equivalent
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Bonferroni-adjusted p=1 is a nonsignificant contrast, not an equivalence test. Their pooled means differ slightly, and the source appropriately says no significant difference.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Higher IB uniquely predicts AI acceptance
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: IB main effect is conditional on the nonalgorithm reference, with no significant IB × algorithm interaction. Do not convert general desirability association into a verified AI-specific moderator.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Both concern algorithm aversion in allocation. The earlier study tests discretion using a rule-based system; the current sparse AI label and measured opacity do not replace that distinction or establish a new opacity-driven mechanism.

Keep impartial beneficence separate from instrumental-harm endorsement. A scalar utilitarian label obscures different attitudes, and participant judgments do not establish actual AI utilitarian reasoning.
Check printed statistics and construct operationalizations without treating one error as proof every result is false. Raw-data absence prevents exact repairs.
Moral response labels, task context and normative correctness are distinct. A pattern of responses is not by itself a proven irrational mechanism or a new ethical principle.

deferred.reason: Proposed research program on lay descriptive/normative beliefs, not a distinct psychological behavior. Preserve it as context rather than a new behavior row.

deferred.term: Opacity-driven algorithm aversion as an independent mechanism
deferred.reason: Post-outcome measured association does not isolate a causal opacity mechanism. Existing Algorithm aversion receives the bounded finding.
Brief secondary bibliography/background without a sufficiently developed new operational definition or original study reading here. Do not turn fear-of-markets shorthand into a verified AI behavior.

deferred.term: New justice principles from the vignette result
deferred.reason: The article discusses existing normative frameworks. Public acceptance and one selected resource contrast do not establish new ethical principles or require new ontology categories.

limitations: Zero new records; four existing concepts receive bounded study/definition evidence and three receive non-counted context. Catalogue remains 782 records across eleven categories. Stable IDs, unnumbered rows, seven evaluation criteria and six ethical principles retained. No automatic harm links, invented annual totals, forced source quota, full-paper Markdown archive or replication claim.
